Instrument.name: The Tunde-M (TNM) Energetic Particle Analyzer for Vega 1
Instrument.description: The Tunde-M (TNM) Energetic Particle Analyzer on Vega 1 and Vega 2 were identical. The primary objective of the TNM was to measure the energy and flux of the cometary ions that might be accelerated by magnetic fields like the solar wind. The TNM comprised two similar telescopes viewing at 55 degrees to the east of the Sun and 90 degrees to the east of the Sun, both in the ecliptic plane and roughly opposite to the spacecraft velocity vector. Each telescope consisted of two silicon detectors, A and B, and an anti-coincidence scintillation shield. Low-energy ions triggered a signal in detector A only. The ion energy range of the TNM "A" detector was 20 to 640 keV. The overall detection range for electrons was 0.5 to 0.75 MeV; for protons 3.2 to 13 MeV, and for ions (Z >= 2) 3.2 to 13 MeV/nucleon.
